target.description: Get US weather forecasts, active alerts, and current observations.

env.name: NWS_USER_AGENT
env.description: User-Agent header for NWS API requests. The API requires this header but a default is provided.

env.name: MCP_LOG_LEVEL
env.description: Sets the minimum log level for output (e.g., 'debug', 'info', 'warn').

checks.summary: Listed in the MCP Registry as io.github.cyanheads/nws-weather-mcp-server.
Repository owner matches GitHub namespace cyanheads.

observation.network_policy: sinkhole: DNS is answered with placeholder addresses and every TCP connection and UDP datagram is captured inside the sandbox; nothing leaves it

tools.name: nws_get_forecast
tools.description: Get the weather forecast for a US location. Returns either named 12-hour periods (default) or hourly breakdowns.

tools.name: nws_search_alerts
tools.description: Search active weather alerts (watches, warnings, advisories) across the US. Filter by state, coordinates, zone, land/marine region, event type, severity, urgency, or certainty. area, point, zone, region_type, and region are mutually exclusive — provide at most one. Omit all filters for a national search.

tools.name: nws_get_alert
tools.description: Fetch one NWS alert message by ID — a current alert, or an earlier message that an update or cancellation has since superseded and that an active-alert search no longer returns. Takes an id from nws_search_alerts or a references[].identifier from any alert, and returns the same alert fields nws_search_alerts does. The message carries its own references, newest first, so a revision chain is walked one call per message. Every reference sharing the newest sent time is an immediate predecessor (an update can merge several earlier segments), so references[0] is one of them, not always the only one.

tools.name: nws_get_alert_counts
tools.description: Count active weather alerts nationwide, per state/territory or marine area, and per marine region, in one small response — the answer to "how many alerts are active, and where" without fetching the alerts themselves. Counts cover every message status, Test and Exercise included, so totalAlerts can run above the totalCount a national nws_search_alerts search reports under its default status of Actual. An alert counts once in each area its zones fall in, so the area counts can sum past totalAlerts; landAlerts plus marineAlerts equals totalAlerts. Takes no filters. For counts per zone or under a

tools.name: nws_get_observations
tools.description: Get current weather observations (actual measured conditions). Accepts coordinates (resolves nearest station automatically) or a station ID directly (e.g., "KSEA").

tools.name: nws_get_observation_history
tools.description: Get a station's recent observation history, newest first — the trend behind the single latest reading nws_get_observations returns (is pressure falling, is the wind picking up). NWS keeps about the last 7 days per station, and a busy airport station reports as often as every 5 minutes, so a day can run past 100 observations: narrow with start (inclusive) and end (exclusive), and page back to older observations with nextCursor. Takes a station ID; use nws_find_stations to find one near a coordinate.

tools.name: nws_find_stations
tools.description: Find weather observation stations near a location. Returns stations sorted by proximity with distance and bearing. Use to discover station IDs for nws_get_observations.

tools.name: nws_list_alert_types
tools.description: List all valid NWS alert event type names. Use to discover valid values for the event filter in nws_search_alerts, or to browse alert categories. No parameters required.

tools.name: nws_get_office_discussion
tools.description: Get the latest narrative forecast product from a Weather Forecast Office (WFO). The default product is AFD (Area Forecast Discussion), which explains the meteorological reasoning behind the forecast — synoptic setup, model guidance, and forecaster confidence. Other types: HWO (Hazardous Weather Outlook, 1-7 day severe/flood/winter outlook), ZFP (Zone Forecast Product, zone-by-zone text), SPS (Special Weather Statement, short-fuse advisory), FWF (Fire Weather Planning Forecast, one segment per fire weather zone). The office code is the 3-letter WFO identifier returned as the "office" field by n

tools.name: nws_get_zone_forecast
tools.description: Get the text forecast for an NWS forecast zone. Returns named forecast periods (e.g., "Today", "Tonight", "Monday") with detailed narrative text — the human-readable, zone-level forecast written by local forecasters. Completes the alert-to-forecast chain: nws_search_alerts returns each affected zone in "affectedZones" as a code plus a type, and nws_find_stations returns codes in the "forecastZone" column. sandbox: Network: container namespace of the sinkhole (no route out).
limits: Install ran in a separate container with unrestricted network access (to fetch the package), with install scripts and source builds disabled.
File reads are not recorded; writes are measured against the freshly installed image.
Writes to tmpfs mounts such as /dev/shm are not visible.
Only tools declared read-only (or named with --safe-tool) were called, with synthetic inputs; every other tool's behaviour is unobserved.
Effects are attributed to the phase in which they appeared; background activity can land in a neighbouring phase.
One short session was observed; delayed or conditional behaviour may not have triggered.
Rewrites of files already changed in an earlier phase are detected by size and modification time while the server runs; a rewrite that keeps both, or one during shutdown, is not seen.
Non-DNS UDP is counted without its destination.

suggestions.title: Pinned launch entry
suggestions.note: Generated from published metadata with the exact version. MCPAudit never reads or edits your client configuration; paste it yourself after review.

suggestions.title: Tool permissions (Claude Code settings)
suggestions.note: allow: declared read-only and called successfully with no effects seen. deny: declared destructive, injection-matching, or a high-severity mismatch. ask: everything not proven either way.

suggestions.title: Network egress
suggestions.body:
review api.weather.gov:443  # attempted during tool:nws_find_stations, tool:nws_list_alert_types
deny *  # nothing else was attempted
suggestions.note: Hosts are attempts recorded by the sinkhole; none were reached. Allow only what the tools you use need.

suggestions.title: Filesystem writes
suggestions.note: Paths are where it wrote during the observed session; reads were not recorded.
